source_findings: systemd-nspawn is a lightweight namespace container that can boot a full Linux userspace/init tree while deliberately restricting access to kernel interfaces, host clock changes, device-node creation, host reboot and kernel-module loading. It therefore has high fidelity for many userspace/service/session lifecycle failures but cannot stand in for a distinct target kernel, firmware or physical device stack.
nspawn supports ephemeral/volatile filesystem modes, making it suitable for cheap repeatable clean-state and dirty-state scenario resets.

network namespaces isolate devices, protocol stacks, routing, firewall state, sockets and related network state; veth pairs provide a deterministic bridge between isolated namespaces. This is a direct fit for HRT network detach/reconnect/rename and fault-surface scenarios.

QEMU VirtIO intentionally supplies generic paravirtualized devices and is recommended when a specific hardware driver is not the object under test. This is useful for guest-kernel/boot/lifecycle testing but is negative evidence against treating a generic VM as a faithful UM790/Radeon/USB4 board replica.

QEMU host CPU passthrough can expose host CPU model/features closely, while KVM may still filter features that virtualization cannot support. CPU passthrough does not establish board, GPU, USB4, firmware or peripheral identity.

dm-flakey is explicitly intended to simulate periodically unreliable storage and can be combined with dm-delay; tc-netem supports delay, loss, corruption, duplication, reordering, rate limiting and a seed for reproducible random impairment. These are strong HRT-L3 fault-injection primitives.

The cheapest high-coverage design is layered rather than monolithic: namespace/container userspace twin for frequent scenarios, VM/kernel twin only when a separate kernel/boot/device model is required, and exact physical host evidence for final host-specific gates.

tier_a_fast_userspace_twin: real systemd service lifecycle inside the container
dm-flakey/dm-delay storage fault injection where safely isolated
tier_b_kernel_boot_twin: QEMU/KVM guest for own kernel, boot/reboot, kernel-version and generic virtual-device paths
prefer VirtIO when the objective is generic OS/device behavior rather than a specific physical driver
tier_c_physical_witness: real UM790 host readback/restart/recovery/soak acceptance where required
f2_distillation.promotion_rule: Tier A or B may increase SIMULATED_HOST_VERIFIED/pre-handoff robustness evidence only. Neither may mint EXACT_HOST_BOUND, REAL_READBACK_VERIFIED, RESTART_RECOVERY_VERIFIED or SOAK_VERIFIED for the physical UM790 unless the corresponding evidence is actually observed on that exact target identity.

counterhypothesis: A single QEMU/KVM image could simplify orchestration enough that the extra startup/RAM cost is outweighed by lower test-harness complexity, making a separate namespace tier unnecessary.
falsifier: Implement an equivalent bounded HRT scenario subset in nspawn and QEMU/KVM and compare startup time, steady RSS, setup complexity, scenario coverage, determinism and false-positive/false-negative host-fidelity findings. If the VM is not materially costlier and covers all namespace-tier cases with equal reproducibility, collapse the tiers.
negative_evidence: No source supports silicon-identical UM790 emulation from generic QEMU/KVM.
No source supports granting physical-host acceptance from namespace or VM simulation alone.
No target-host fingerprint from the real UM790 was observed in this research objective.
